properties.state: {"decision":"Anthony, 2026-09-05: yes. The derived scans that every orientation rollup recomputes - open_defects (~5.2-5.8 s, ten call sites) and detect_gaps (~1.5 s) - are memoised, keyed on a write generation counter. Core has no such counter today; it gains one, bumped at the ONE place every mutation passes through, engine/batch.rs:44 commit_batch, so no write path can be missed. The optimize skill warns that a cache is a global and a rule traded for speed; the case for this one is stated here rather than waved through: (1) the pattern is already accepted in this codebase - service.rs:3731 is a write_gen-keyed cache - so this reuses a precedent rather than introducing one; (2) invalidation is at a single choke point, not scattered; (3) the memo holds a DERIVED result over a graph state, never a source of truth, so a stale entry can only ever be a stale count, never lost design. What is NOT decided: whether other derived rollups (the SPOF analysis, granularity) join the memo. One thing at a time, re-measured.","kind":"choice","name":"DECIDED - open_defects and detect_gaps are memoised per write generation, invalidated at the single commit choke point","rationale":"The alternative - making each scan faster - was rejected because the measurement shows the cost is repetition, not the scan: the same result is derived three times per orientation pass and once more on every read after a write.
